subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = 1/(6x − x² − 5).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.12, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 19 part (a-i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the conditions the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find where the denominator is zero
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Write it before any factorising.
steps.memory_tip: No root and no logarithm here, only a denominator. Set it equal to zero and remove those points.
lines: f(x) is not defined when 6x − x² − 5 = 0

recall.must_convey: That only the denominator can fail, so the work is to solve 6x − x² − 5 = 0 and get x = 1 and x = 5.
accept: the denominator must not be zero so solve six x minus x squared minus five equals zero
multiply by minus one to get x squared minus six x plus five and factorise
the bottom is zero at one and five so those two go out
denominator zero ayye chotla function undadu so one and five theeyali
set the denominator equal to zero and get the roots one and five
heard_as: six x minus x squared minus five
x squared minus six x plus five

steps.why: The numerator is the constant 1, so the only way the formula can fail is a zero denominator. Rearranging to x² − 6x + 5 puts the quadratic in the form that factorises directly.
common_mistakes: Solving 6x − x² − 5 > 0, which is the condition for a square root, not for a denominator.
A sign slip when rearranging −x² + 6x − 5 into x² − 6x + 5.

steps.label: Remove those points from R
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.
steps.memory_tip: Two roots removed, so the answer is R minus a set of two numbers, never an inequality.
lines: For all other x the denominator is not zero.
So x may be any real number except 1 and 5.

recall.must_convey: That the domain is every real number except 1 and 5.
accept: all real numbers except one and five
R minus the set one and five
minus infinity to one union one to five union five to infinity
one and five thappa anni real numbers
every real except the two roots of the denominator
heard_as: six x minus x squared minus five
x squared minus six x plus five

steps.why: Each root of the denominator removes exactly one point from the real line, so two roots leave a line with two holes in it.
common_mistakes: Reporting {1, 5} as the domain instead of what is removed from R.
Writing R − [1, 5], which wrongly removes the whole interval between them.
